exam.title: Art Paper 1 (33/1) - October/November 2022
exam.subject: Art
exam.description: Botswana Examinations Council, Junior Certificate Examination. Answer all 40 questions. Four possible answers are given for each; choose the one you think is correct.

questions.question: The area between and within components of a composition in art is referred to as
questions.explanation: Space is the art element describing the area within and around the components of a composition.

questions.question: Which picture below depicts calmness?
questions.explanation: The flowing, serene silhouette of the face in B evokes calm, unlike the crying emoji (A), raised hands in distress (C), or roaring lion (D).

questions.question: Which of the following art forms can be regarded as pre-historic?
questions.explanation: Rock art (paintings and engravings on rock surfaces) is one of the earliest known art forms, dating back to pre-historic times.

questions.question: Which of the following is a set of oil paint vehicles?
questions.explanation: Thinners and turpentine are the vehicles (liquid mediums) traditionally used to thin and work with oil paint; water is not compatible with oil paint.

questions.question: The sculpture below was made by modelling. Which of the materials below are suitable for making the sculpture?
questions.explanation: Modelling uses soft, pliable materials that can be shaped by hand -- wax and clay -- unlike stone and wood, which are carved.

questions.question: Which of the following fabric patterns is random?
questions.explanation: A and B are regular, repeating tiled motifs and C is a structured density gradient; D is made of continuous, non-repeating flowing lines with no fixed tiling unit, making it the most random/organic of the four.

questions.question: Which set of tools below can be used in print making?
questions.explanation: A roller (brayer) spreads ink and a squeegee pushes ink through a screen -- both standard print making tools.

questions.question: Which of the images below is a logo?
questions.explanation: A is a self-contained circular monogram mark designed to represent a brand, whereas B is a QR code and C/D are full movie posters.

questions.question: What type of proportion does the image below depict?
questions.explanation: The figure has an elongated neck and stretched body far beyond natural human proportions, which is an exaggeration.

questions.question: Which weaving technique was used to make the basket pictured below?
questions.explanation: The basket's spiralling, stacked rings of woven material are characteristic of the coiling technique.

questions.question: Which of the following tools is used to apply wax when making batik?
questions.explanation: A tjanting (canting) is the traditional pen-like tool used to apply hot wax in batik work.

questions.question: Which of the following images shows a promotional poster?
questions.explanation: A is a clear event invitation (BBQ Party) designed to promote an event, while B is a book cover, C a novelty decal, and D a home decor print.

questions.question: Which of the materials below are suitable for making stencils in print making?
questions.explanation: Cardboard, potato and lino can all be cut and used to create stencil/printing blocks, unlike the loose or unsuitable materials in the other options.

questions.question: What is the role of a book illustrator?
options: Advices on the prices of books
questions.explanation: A book illustrator creates the drawings/images that accompany and support the text in a book.

questions.question: Which of the following images effectively shows perspective?
questions.explanation: The landscape in A uses converging lines and diminishing scale toward the horizon -- classic linear perspective -- while B, C and D are flat, stylised or non-perspectival.

questions.question: Use the picture below to answer questions 16 and 17. Which art principle references the relationship in size between the two animals?
questions.explanation: Proportion is the art principle concerned with the relative size relationship between elements, such as the lion and the cub.

questions.question: Which two art elements were effectively used in the picture?
questions.explanation: The drawing relies heavily on tonal shading (value) to render the fur's texture, making these the two most prominent elements at work.

questions.question: Which of the following tools can be used in painting?
questions.explanation: Palette knives, sponges and brushes are all genuine tools used to apply paint; clippers are not a painting tool.

questions.question: Which of the art Masters listed below was an abstract expressionist?
questions.explanation: Jackson Pollock is one of the most iconic abstract expressionist painters, known for his drip-painting technique.

questions.question: What is the name given to a painting technique which results in a semi-transparent layers of colour on a surface?
questions.explanation: A wash is a thin, diluted application of paint that produces a semi-transparent layer of colour.

questions.question: Use the image of an artefact below to answer question 21. Which form of art is depicted by the image?
questions.explanation: The pictured necklace is a piece of jewellery.

questions.question: What type of artwork does the picture below represent?
questions.explanation: The segmented, leaded outline of the peacock is characteristic of a stained glass design.

questions.question: Which of the following statements describes the term maquette?
options: It is a large sculptural form.
It is a model for a sculpture.
It is an artwork sold at the market.
It is a small piece of craft meant for decoration.
questions.explanation: A maquette is a small preliminary model made by a sculptor to plan a larger final sculpture.

questions.question: A relief sculpture
options: shows a head of an animal.
stands out from a flat surface.
can be viewed from all angles.
is made from a pliable material.
questions.explanation: A relief sculpture is carved so that the forms project out from, but remain attached to, a flat background.

questions.question: What effect is brought about by adding white to a colour?
questions.explanation: Adding white to a colour produces a tint, which lightens and brightens the colour.

questions.question: What name is given to the process of making a clay pot using a potter's wheel?
questions.explanation: Shaping clay on a spinning potter's wheel is called throwing.

questions.question: Which image below is not ceramic?
questions.explanation: The horse figure in A has the smooth, metallic sheen of a cast bronze/metal sculpture, unlike the ceramic vases (C, D) and the woven ball (B), which is also non-ceramic but the horse is the intended distractor here.

questions.question: Which statement below is a definition of pointilism?
options: It is the use of small lines to show emphasis.
It is shading using arrows that leads one to a focal point.
It is a shading technique which uses dots to form an image.
It is when arrows direct viewers to an object in a composition.
questions.explanation: Pointillism is a technique where small, distinct dots of colour are applied to form an image.

questions.question: Which of the following is a print making technique that involves the passing of ink through a mesh onto a surface?
questions.explanation: Screen printing forces ink through a fine mesh screen onto the surface below.

questions.question: Which of the following is a set of threads interlaced at right angles when weaving?
questions.explanation: The warp (vertical threads) and weft (horizontal threads) are interlaced at right angles in weaving.

questions.question: Use the image below to answer question 31. The image represents a
questions.explanation: The butter box shown is a product package, so this is an example of package design.

questions.question: Use the image of a costume below to answer question 32. Which art principle is more visible in the image?
questions.explanation: The repeated, layered feather shapes on each wing create a strong sense of rhythm.

questions.question: In indigenous Africa, art was more about
questions.explanation: Indigenous African art was deeply tied to expressing the customs, beliefs and values of the people who made it.

questions.question: Use the picture below to answer question 34. What is the purpose of the tool pictured above?
options: It is used to break ink lumps.
It breaks the inked surface into textural effects.
It is used to spread ink evenly on a printing plate.
It separates ink particles according to their colour classes.
questions.explanation: The pictured tool is a brayer/roller, used to spread ink evenly across a printing plate or block.

questions.question: What do portraits X, Y and Z below demostrate?
options: X: Mood, Y: Line, Z: Space
X: Bust, Y: Texture, Z: Age
X: Texture, Y: Contour, Z: Mood
X: Mood, Y: Proportion, Z: Value
questions.explanation: X shows strong emotional mood, Y is a construction drawing showing facial proportion guidelines, and Z uses tonal shading (value) to render aged, wrinkled skin.

questions.question: Use the image of a stamp below to answer question 36. Which of the following is likely to be the theme of the stamp?
questions.explanation: The stamp depicts a Cattle Egret, a specific bird species, with its name and "Botswana" printed on it -- matching the theme Birds of Botswana most precisely.

questions.question: Which of the images below is not fit as a billboard?
questions.explanation: A is an abstract paint-splash composition with no clear advertising message, while B, C and D are all structured adverts suited to billboard format.

questions.question: Which art principle was effectively achieved in the picture below?
questions.explanation: The star pattern is symmetrically arranged around a central point, achieving visual balance.

questions.question: Which of the phrases below is not true about clay slip?
options: Used as a bonding agent for clay pieces
Used to hand build clay coils for ceramic pots
Poured into a mould to cast ceramic or clay items
questions.explanation: Coils used in hand-building are rolled from solid clay, not built from slip; slip is instead used to decorate, bond pieces together, or for slip-casting -- making the coil-building claim the false statement.

questions.question: Which set of materials below can be used in casting?
questions.explanation: Wax, bronze, plaster and concrete are all genuine casting materials (as in lost-wax bronze casting and plaster/concrete moulding).
